retained_original_metadata.title: Twisted equivariant K-theory of compact finite-group spaces with a trivially acting normal subgroup decomposes over projective-representation orbits with explicit quotient cocycles
retained_original_metadata.author: José Manuel Gómez; Johana Ramírez
retained_original_metadata.source_title: A Decomposition of Twisted Equivariant K-Theory
retained_original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs the quotient twisting cocycle from projective intertwining operators and checks its cocycle law explicitly. It then builds mutually inverse isotypic Hom and tensor constructions and assembles the orbit blocks through finite-index bundle induction. The resulting quotient twists and their actions are essential data; untwisted representation decomposition alone does not produce the claimed natural K-theory isomorphism.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Complete selected author Theorem3.7 route is supplied: normal A in finite G, compact Hausdorff G-space X on which A acts trivially, normalized unit-circle2-cocycle alpha on G. The action on Irr_alpha(A), stabilizers G_[tau]/A, and explicit beta_(tau,alpha) formula2.3 are preserved. The new cocycle computation2.8 and the projective Hom/tensor action calculations3.4 are written;3.6 gives the orbit-block actions and the finite direct-sum inverse bundle LF. Although Section3 calls these proofs sketches/outlines, it supplies the new projective action formulas, cocycle compatibility and inverse evaluation constructions. The unexpanded finite-index induced-bundle equivariance is the standard ordinary induction for the central-extension group and is explicitly referred to the established untwisted construction [6]; no new projective core is inferred from that pointer alone. The statement is functorial K-theory with the specified constant group-cocycle twists, not arbitrary topological gerbes or compact Lie groups. Spectral-sequence and dihedral examples are contextual only.
